rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at moderate temperature to reveal the full elution window and whether any compounds are unretained or still retained at 42 min. This gives a balanced first map of retention and selectivity before trimming the gradient window or changing slope.

All compounds are already fully resolved, so the score is now limited only by time; the goal is to keep full resolution while pulling the last peak under 10 min. The first run suggests the useful elution window is roughly phi 0.11 to 0.41, so a trimmed, steeper gradient centered on that region should compress the chromatogram without making the early peak unretained.

We still have full resolution margin, so push for speed by slightly steepening the gradient and raising temperature to reduce retention, especially of the late isolated last peak. The wider upper endpoint helps ensure that last compound elutes within the gradient rather than lingering into the hold.

The last run reached the no-time-penalty region, so the only remaining gain is to recover the single under-resolved pair while staying under 10 min. Keeping the same phi window and temperature but making the gradient slightly shallower should selectively improve the slope-sensitive 6/7 pair with only a modest increase in t_last.

The 6/7 pair got worse when only tG was lengthened, suggesting it is not slope-driven and is more likely temperature/selectivity-sensitive. Step temperature down slightly while keeping the fast successful window from injection 3 to try to improve that pair’s selectivity while remaining under 10 min.

The critical pair is strongly temperature-sensitive, and lowering T collapsed it, so test the opposite direction with a modestly cooler-start/narrower window to shift selectivity around the middle of the chromatogram while keeping the run fast. This probes whether a higher temperature plus slightly lower effective phi around peaks 6/7 can push that pair above 1.5 without reintroducing a time penalty.

We are very close to the maximum, with only pair 4/5 slightly below full credit and plenty of time margin under 10 min. A small increase in tG at the same temperature and window is the lowest-risk way to try to lift that pair above 1.5 while likely keeping t_last under 10 min.

Injection 7 achieved full resolution but barely missed the 10 min target, so now the aim is to preserve that selectivity while nudging the last peak earlier. Raising only phi1 slightly should shorten the late tail and last peak more than the earlier cluster, with a good chance of keeping all pairs at or above 1.5.

We have already reached the maximum CRF, so the best strategy is to confirm whether an even faster method can keep the same perfect score. Shortening tG while holding the successful window and temperature tests for a shorter equivalent optimum, with injection 8 retained as the fallback.

A perfect method is already in hand, so this is a low-risk local probe to see whether slightly higher phi1 can shorten the late region further while preserving the fully resolved pattern. The critical pair appears earlier and mainly responds to slope/selectivity, so a modest increase in the upper endpoint may leave resolution intact.

With a perfect method already achieved, use a nearby temperature probe to test whether a small further selectivity shift can maintain full resolution while possibly reducing retention more. The critical pairs are temperature-sensitive, so 60 C is the most informative adjacent setting around the current optimum.

The optimum is already known, so this is a targeted local test of whether lowering phi0 slightly can improve the early/mid selectivity around the 4/5 pair without costing the time goal. Since the first peak is still retained at 0.80 min in the optimum run, there is room to move the start composition lower.

Use the fully resolved 0.15 to 0.55 window and make the gradient slightly longer than injection 7 to see whether extra slope relief improves the margin on the critical early/mid pairs enough to offset the likely small time increase. This is a close local probe around the optimum that may still keep the last peak near 10 min while testing robustness of full resolution in a narrower window.

A perfect method is already secured, so this is a final nearby robustness check around the optimum by slightly lengthening the same successful window. It tests whether full resolution is retained with a little extra spacing, while injection 8 remains the benchmark if time penalty appears.

With the optimum already found, test whether a slightly higher starting composition can further compress the front of the chromatogram while preserving full resolution and keeping the last peak under 10 min. This is the main untested one-step local variant around injection 8.

A perfect method is already secured, so use one remaining nearby temperature point to map robustness on the low side of the optimum. The strong temperature sensitivity of the critical pairs makes 50 C the most informative missing local check around the winning method.

The remaining useful local corner near the optimum is to lower both phi0 and phi1 together, keeping slope similar while shifting the whole elution window to slightly lower phi. This tests whether the critical pair balance can be improved without losing the sub-10 min last peak, although injection 8 already remains the winner.

The current best is already perfect, so use remaining injections to complete the local map of the narrower fast window at high temperature. This checks whether the strong temperature effect seen at 0.15/0.60/10 also applies in the 8 min, lower-phi1 regime and helps define sensitivity boundaries around the optimum.

Use a remaining injection to test the opposite combined window shift from injection 17: lower phi0 but higher phi1 around the proven 10 min, 55 C setting. This keeps the window broad while probing whether early retention and late acceleration can coexist without disturbing the critical pair balance.

A second perfect method is now available, so test whether this broader successful window can be shortened to 8 min while retaining full resolution. If it works, it would identify an even faster robust family, while the 10 min versions remain proven optima.

With two perfect methods already found, probe whether a slightly higher phi1 on the broader successful window can preserve full resolution while pulling the latest region still earlier. This is a low-risk local extension from injection 19, and the main value is mapping the robustness plateau around the perfect conditions.

You now have a clear plateau of perfect methods as phi1 increases, so extend that trend one more step to find the upper edge of the robustness window and possibly a still shorter last peak. This is the most informative remaining local move because it changes only one factor from a perfect method.

The perfect-method plateau continues through phi1 0.75, so one more step upward is the cleanest way to locate the robustness boundary while potentially shortening the last peak further. This keeps all other factors fixed on the established optimum family.

The upper boundary in phi1 has begun to erode the 4/5 pair, so use a remaining injection to test whether lowering phi0 can recover margin while keeping the successful phi1 0.75 setting and fast last peak. This explores another corner of the perfect plateau with only one substantial change in the early gradient region.

For the final shot, target the center of the newly mapped perfect plateau between phi1 0.65 to 0.75 while keeping the lower phi0 that also gave a perfect score. This should give a robust fully resolved method with the critical pair likely a bit safer than at 0.75 and still a short last peak.
